https://www.london-now.co.uk/news/266331.text: Leisure Travel London day out cost - Fifth most expensive city in Europe Leisure Travel By Holly Brencher Reporter Share 0 Comments London has been named Europe's fifth most expensive city for sightseeing (Image: Canva) This article is brought to you by our exclusive subscriber partnership with our sister title USA Today, and has been written by our American colleagues. It does not necessarily reflect the view of The Herald. London has been named the fifth most expensive city in Europe for a day out, with visitors spending an average of £118.37 on food, drinks, transport and sightseeing. This puts a day in the capital above the widely used £100 daily budget r ecommended for comfortable travel. The findings come from a new study by InsureandGo, which calculated the cost of a typical day out—including two meals, drinks, public transport, and entry to a top attraction— in more than 120 European cities. A costly day out The research found that other UK cities also exceed the £100 mark, including Edinburgh (£104.45), Bristol (£103.80), and Liverpool (£101.29). Read more You can meet Father Christmas in the sky above London this year Londoners can party among dinosaurs and skeletons after dark this Halloween The £850,000 gap between London's cheapest and most expensive boroughs Hyde Park Winter Wonderland returns with £1 entry and new K-Pop circus In contrast, the most affordable city in Europe was Skopje, North Macedonia, where a full day out costs just £28.80. Mellisa Hutchins, travel cover specialist at InsureandGo, said: "Our study shows that across most of Europe, a daily budget of £100 still covers a full day of eating out and sightseeing, and in some cities across Central Europe around half that amount is plenty. "Regardless of where you’re heading, plan your budget before you go. "Check local prices for food and drinks but also look for free attractions and make the most of public transport. "One place not to cut costs is your travel insurance. "Unexpected medical bills or cancellations can easily wipe out a holiday budget, so comprehensive travel cover helps you relax and enjoy your trip. "There are still plenty of places left to discover this year, and we hope this research inspires you to visit somewhere new that aligns with your budget." Comparing cities The average day out across Europe costs £78, according to the research. However, the study found wide variation in costs, with Reykjavik, Iceland, topping the list as the most expensive city at £145.33 per day. This is more than five times the daily cost of Skopje. The top five most expensive cities in Europe were Reykjavik (£145.33), Zurich (£132.11), Basel (£125.12), Bern (£121.22), and London (£118.37). Coventry was named the most affordable UK city, with a daily cost of £67.64, well below the European average. Other UK cities close to the £100 threshold include Manchester (£98.75) and Brighton (£98.36). Budget-friendly destinations Several European cities still offer excellent value for money. Chisinau, Moldova, was the second cheapest city at £35.52 per day. Sarajevo, Bosnia and Herzegovina, followed in third place at £38.52. Other affordable destinations under £50 per day include Tirana, Albania (£44.96), and Belgrade, Serbia (£46.99). Central European cities such as Brașov, Romania (£47.23), and Poznań, Poland (£47.51), also featured in the top 10 most affordable destinations. For travellers seeking warmer weather, Porto was the most budget-friendly option at £53.65 per day. Alicante (£55.28) and Málaga (£55.44) in Spain also made the list. Free and low-cost travel Several destinations stand out not only for their low overall costs but for specific budget-friendly features. Belgrade, for example, offers free public transport, while Skopje boasts the cheapest entry fee to a top attraction—a cable car ride to the Millennium Cross costs just £1.39. Chisinau is an ideal base for exploring Moldova’s famous wine country, with public transport costing as little as 60 pence for a return journey. Visitors to Sarajevo can enjoy lunch for just £6.59, with a three-course dinner averaging £15.36. The city’s Baščaršija quarter, known for its blend of Ottoman and Austro-Hungarian architecture, offers a rich cultural experience at an affordable price. Travel tips Ms Hutchins encouraged travellers to research their destinations in advance to get the most value from their trips. She advised looking for free attractions, making use of public transport, and prioritising travel insurance to avoid unexpected costs. She also emphasised that a daily budget of £100 remains reasonable in many European cities, though some will require more careful planning. https://arynews.tv/ram-charans-productio.text: Lifestyle Ram Charan’s production 'The India House' unveils Saiee Manjrekar’s new look By Sarah Brohi - Oct 28, 2026 Add ARY News on Google Follow on Google Discover Instagram A A Resize Bollywood actress Saiee M Manjrekar is all set to explore a new on-screen role with The India House. Ram Charan is set to produce the action-drama film. A photograph reportedly taken during the film’s ongoing shoot in Estonia has offered a glimpse of the actress in character, generating curiosity about her role in the historical drama. In the image, Saiee is seen wearing a white, full-sleeved blouse paired with a floor-length maroon skirt, dark stockings, and white shoes. With her hair left open, the actress holds a flaming torch above her head, while what appears to be a protest banner can be seen in the background. Her look and intense expression suggest a character associated with the political unrest and revolutionary activities explored in the film. The appearance marked a departure from Saiee’s previous screen outings, with her styling reflecting the period in which the story is set. While the makers have yet to officially reveal the details of her character, the photograph has offered an early indication of the world the film seeks to recreate. A source close to the production shared, “Saiee’s character in India House is quite different from what audiences have seen her do before. Her look is rooted in the period, and the image captures the spirit of a character who appears to stand for something bigger than herself. There is a certain intensity to her role, and audiences will get to see a new side of her as an actor.” Lifestyle News – Latest Entertainment News, Celebrity Gossip Directed by debutant filmmaker Ram Vamsi Krishna, The India House features Nikhil Siddhartha as the male lead along with Saiee M Manjrekar as the female lead, with Anupam Kher in leading roles. Kher portrays Shyamji Krishna Varma, the Indian nationalist and revolutionary thinker whose activities played a significant role in the country’s freedom movement. Set in London around 1905, the film draws inspiration from the historic India House, a student residence that became an important centre for Indian nationalists and revolutionaries living in Britain. The establishment provided a platform for discussions on India’s independence and became associated with several figures involved in the anti-colonial movement. Against this historical backdrop, The India House combines a love story with the growing revolutionary movement among Indians living abroad. The narrative is expected to explore the personal relationships and political circumstances unfolding during a significant period in the country’s struggle for independence. The project is being produced by Ram Charan under his banner V Mega Pictures, alongside Abhishek Agarwal of Abhishek Agarwal Arts and Vikram Reddy. The film is among the projects backed by Charan as he continues to expand his involvement in film production beyond his work as an actor. The production has been filming across Indian and international locations, with Estonia serving as one of its European shooting destinations. The overseas schedule is expected to help recreate the historical setting of early 20th-century London, which forms the backdrop for the story. Positioned as a pan-India project, The India House is being developed for release in multiple Indian languages. Its combination of historical events, period drama, action and romance places the film within a genre that has continued to attract interest from filmmakers and audiences alike. The film is targeting a theatrical release in late 2026 or 2027. Further details about the characters, the story and the release schedule are awaited as production progresses.
